# Entra Security Baseline — A Federal AD-to-Entra Crosswalk {.unnumbered}

::: {.callout-note}
## In this reference

Microsoft's [Configure Microsoft Entra for increased security](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/fundamentals/configure-security) page lists ~150 hardening controls grouped under the **Secure Future Initiative (SFI)** and Zero-Trust pillars, each tagged with a minimum license. That page is written for a **commercial workforce tenant** and is silent on the two things that decide what a federal agency can actually do: **government-cloud availability** and **20 years of Active Directory entanglement**.

This reference re-scores every theme through that federal lens. Each control gets four added columns — **minimum license → GCC-Moderate availability → AD-friction → effort tier** — so you can read it as a sequencing plan, not just a checklist. [Annex A](#annex-a-zero-trust-assessment-federal-usability) covers the companion automation (the **Zero Trust Assessment** PowerShell module) and its real behavior against government tenants.

This document is **pedagogical** — a planning and learning artifact for architects and assessors. It is not a runbook and assumes no dry-run against a production agency tenant.
:::

## 1. The assessment in one paragraph

A 20-year AD agency on **GCC Moderate** can implement a meaningful slice of the SFI baseline **quickly** — the consent/guest/logging/break-glass/legacy-auth/PIM cluster is mostly Free/P1/P2, already licensed under M365 **G5**, and config-only. But three filters knock out or defer roughly a third of the page before any work starts: the **entire "Protect networks" theme is Global Secure Access**, which is **unavailable in GCC High/DoD and non-FIPS in GCC Moderate**; the **AI theme** is nascent and unconfirmed in gov; and the heaviest identity controls (**managed-device sign-in, token protection, org-wide phishing-resistant auth, cloud authentication**) are gated on **device, Intune, and federation modernization** that two decades of AD make a multi-quarter program rather than a toggle. The agency's one structural advantage is **PIV/CAC → Entra Certificate-Based Authentication (CBA)**, which turns several "project" phishing-resistant controls into "accelerated."

## 2. The three filters

### Filter 1 — Government-cloud eligibility

| Theme | GCC-Moderate reality |
|---|---|
| Protect identities & secrets | Almost entirely **available** (Entra ID, PIM, ID Protection, CBA, Authentication Methods, Password Protection all parity in GCC). |
| Protect tenants | Available. |
| **Protect networks** | **Global Secure Access (Internet Access / Private Access).** **Not available in GCC High / DoD at all.** In **GCC Moderate it runs but is not FIPS 140-2 certified** (it is FedRAMP-High accredited) — an ATO consideration for a federal boundary. Treat as *evaluate*, not *quick win*. |
| Protect engineering systems | Available. |
| Monitor & detect | Available, except the GSA-dependent network-log checks. |
| Accelerate response | Available (Workload ID is a separate SKU; confirm gov entitlement). |
| **AI (Entra Agent ID)** | **Nascent; gov availability unconfirmed — defer.** |

> Availability shifts as gov parity advances. Verify every code below against the authoritative
> [Microsoft Entra feature availability in Azure for US Government](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/feature-availability)
> and the [Global Secure Access certifications](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/global-secure-access/reference-global-secure-access-certifications) page. Codes here are current as of **June 2026**.

### Filter 2 — Licensing

Federal agencies typically run **M365 G5**, which includes **Entra ID P2** (PIM, ID Protection, access reviews, entitlement management). So P1/P2/PIM items are *licensed*; the constraint is operational, not entitlement. The **Internet Access / Private Access / Entra Suite / Workload ID** tags are *separate SKUs* — and collide with Filter 1 anyway.

### Filter 3 — 20-year AD friction

The same control can be a 10-minute toggle or a 9-month program depending on the hybrid estate (Entra Connect sync, ADFS federation, basic-auth LOB apps, decades of service accounts and app registrations, AD-joined-not-Entra-joined devices, on-prem GPO password policy). The **AD-friction** column names that entanglement; the **effort tier** prices it.

## 3. How to read the crosswalk

**Minimum license** — `Free` · `P1` · `P2` · or a separate SKU (`Internet Access`, `Private Access`, `Suite`, `Workload ID`, `ID Governance`).

**GCC-Moderate availability**

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| ✅ | Available in GCC Moderate today |
| ⚠️ | Available but caveated (depends on non-FIPS GSA, or only partial in gov) |
| ❌ | Not available in gov (GCC High/DoD); in GCC Moderate only via non-FIPS GSA |

**AD-friction**

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 🟢 | Cloud-only — no on-prem entanglement |
| 🟡 | Hybrid-touching — coordinate with sync / devices / users |
| 🔴 | Legacy-blocking — gated on retiring or modernizing a 20-year dependency |

**Effort tier**

| Tier | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **T0** | This week. Tenant toggle, no legacy dependency. |
| **T1** | Quick (days). Config is fast; discovery / coordination / rollout is the work. |
| **T2** | Weeks. Inventory + remediation, or staged rollout. |
| **T3** | Multi-quarter program. Gated on device / identity / federation modernization. |
| **—** | Not applicable / not available in your cloud. |

## 6. Crosswalk — Protect networks (mostly out-of-cloud)

::: {.callout-warning}
## The whole theme is Global Secure Access — handle as a gated evaluation, not a quick win

All ~40 checks in [zero-trust-protect-networks](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/fundamentals/zero-trust-protect-networks) belong to **Microsoft Entra Internet Access / Private Access (Global Secure Access)** except the handful of Conditional-Access primitives below. GSA is **❌ not available in GCC High/DoD** and **⚠️ non-FIPS in GCC Moderate**. To keep this crosswalk honest, the GSA family is **collapsed into one row** rather than reproduced as 35+ near-identical "—" entries; the originals are enumerated on the source page.
:::

| Control (or family) | License | GCC | AD-friction | Tier |
|---|---|:--:|:--:|:--:|
| Named locations are configured | P1 | ✅ | 🟢 | **T0→T1** |
| Tenant restrictions v2 policy is configured | P1 | ⚠️ *(header-based works; universal enforcement needs GSA)* | 🟡 | **T2** |
| Conditional Access policies use compliant-network controls | P1 | ⚠️ *(compliant network = GSA signaling)* | 🔴 | **—** until GSA |
| **All GSA families** — Internet Access, Private Access, GSA client, TLS inspection, web-content filtering, threat-intel & file-transfer policy, AI gateway, cloud firewall, Universal CAE, universal tenant restrictions, private connectors/DNS, Quick Access, app segments, DC-RDP protection | Internet/Private Access / Suite | ❌ *(GCC High/DoD)* / ⚠️ *(non-FIPS GCC Moderate)* | — | **—** *(evaluate against ATO; not "quick")* |

## 10. Crosswalk — AI (defer)

::: {.callout-note}
The [AI theme](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/fundamentals/zero-trust-ai) (Entra **Agent ID** controls — authentication to agents, CA over agent identities, custom security attributes, agent-identity governance and ownership) is **nascent and its government-cloud availability is unconfirmed**. **Defer the entire theme** unless the agency is actively standing up Entra Agent ID. Revisit at the `lifecycle_review` date.
:::

## 11. Recommended quick-win sequence

Pulling the **T0/T1** rows into an execution order. License in brackets; all assume GCC-Moderate availability ✅.

1. **Break-glass accounts** [P1] — prerequisite for every Conditional Access change. *(§7)*
2. **Diagnostic settings → Sentinel** [P1] and **ID Protection notifications** [P2] — turn on visibility before you start changing posture. *(§8)*
3. **Consent + guest hardening bundle** [Free] — restrict user consent, enable admin-consent workflow, guests-can't-invite-guests, restricted directory access, disable guest self-sign-up, limit tenant creation. *(§4, §5)*
4. **Tenant-config toggles** [Free] — devices/user ≤ 10, restrict non-admin BitLocker recovery, app instance property lock. *(§5, §7)*
5. **Password & lockout hygiene** [P1] — disable security questions, block admins from SSPR, smart-lockout ≤10 / ≥60s, banned-password org terms (+ on-prem agent), disable password expiration (note GPO caveat). *(§4)*
6. **Migrate to converged authentication-methods policy** [P1] — deadline-driven; enable TAP (single-use), passkey/security-key methods. *(§4)*
7. **Block legacy authentication** [P1] — **staged**: report-only Conditional Access → sign-in-log discovery of basic-auth LOB apps and service accounts → enforce. Highest value, highest legacy risk. *(§4, §8)*
8. **Stand up PIM** [P2] — JIT activation, GA approval workflow, activation alerts, stale-privileged-identity reviews. *(§4, §7, §8)*
9. **Risk-based Conditional Access** [P2] — restrict high-risk users and sign-ins; begin SOC triage cadence. *(§9)*
10. **Phishing-resistant for admins via PIV/CAC → CBA** [P1] — the federal accelerator; start with privileged accounts, then expand. *(§4)*

Everything tagged **T2/T3** (app-credential hygiene, LAPS, cloud-only admin tiering, ADFS→cloud-auth, managed-device sign-in, token protection, org-wide phishing-resistant, PAW) is **real program work** — sequence it into the modernization track, don't promise it as "quick."

## Annex A — Zero Trust Assessment: federal usability {#annex-a-zero-trust-assessment-federal-usability}

Microsoft pairs the checklist with an automated checker — the **Zero Trust Assessment** ([overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/security/zero-trust/assessment/overview) · [get-started](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/security/zero-trust/assessment/get-started)). It is the "operationalize this checklist" tool the configure-security page points to. Here is what it is and how it actually behaves in a government tenant.

### A.1 What it is

An **open-source PowerShell module** (`ZeroTrustAssessment`, [GitHub](https://github.com/microsoft/zerotrustassessment)) that runs **read-only** against a tenant and produces a local HTML report (`ZeroTrustReport\ZeroTrustAssessmentReport.html`) with **Overview / Identity / Devices / Network / Data** tabs, scoring each test by **Risk** and **Status**. Checks are drawn from **NIST / CISA / CIS**, Microsoft's internal baselines, and customer telemetry — the same catalog behind the crosswalk above.

### A.2 Architecture / data handling (the assessor-relevant facts)

- **Read-only, runs locally, fully open source** — nothing is written back to the tenant; assessors can review the code. Strong for an ATO conversation.
- **Stores sensitive tenant data on the local disk** (uses a local **DuckDB** database). Docs explicitly warn the output is attacker-grade intel — **treat the folder as sensitive (CUI-equivalent) and delete it after**. This is a data-handling decision, not a casual desktop run.
- **Large tenants can take 24+ hours.** Requires **PowerShell 7** and the **VC++ 2015-2022 redistributable**; **no ARM64 support**.

### A.3 What it costs to run (the access ask is the real gate)

- **First run requires a Global Administrator** to consent the Microsoft Graph PowerShell app to ~20 read scopes (`AuditLog.Read.All`, `Directory.Read.All`, `Policy.Read.All`, `RoleManagement.Read.All`, `IdentityRisk*.Read.All`, `NetworkAccess.Read.All`, etc.). In a locked-down federal tenant, **standing up a new app consent is itself a governance gate** — usually the hardest step.
- **Subsequent runs** need **Global Reader + Security Reader + Exchange Administrator + SharePoint Administrator**, plus an optional Azure sign-in (skip it and it drops only the log-export check).
- It fans out beyond Entra — **Graph, Azure, Exchange, SharePoint, AIP**.

### A.4 Government-cloud reality

A `-Environment USGov` switch **exists**, so gov is *attempted* — but it is **not clean**, and neither Learn page makes any supportability statement about GCC/GCC High/DoD:

- **[Issue #378 — GCC High](https://github.com/microsoft/zerotrustassessment/issues/378)**: `Connect-ZtAssessment -Environment USGov` fails on `servicePrincipalSignInActivities` (**400 — endpoint not present in gov Graph**), cascading into a DuckDB binder error. **Closed without a documented fix.**
- Many checks are **meaningless in gov anyway** — the entire **Network** tab and scopes like `NetworkAccess.Read.All` map to **Global Secure Access**, which doesn't exist in GCC High/DoD and is non-FIPS in GCC Moderate. Expect those to error or mislead.

**Verdict for GCC Moderate:** the `USGov` path may run further than it does for GCC High, but expect **broken checks and false signal in Network/Data**, and **no Microsoft support commitment**. This is a *read-every-result-with-a-gov-filter* tool, not a clean compliance score.

### A.5 How to use it in a federal program

Since the agency cannot dry-run against production, the durable value is the **check catalog as a learning/crosswalk source**, not the live dashboard:

1. Treat the repo's [test definitions](https://github.com/microsoft/zerotrustassessment/tree/main/src/powershell) as the machine-readable twin of §4–§10 above.
2. If it is run, do so from a **commercial-equivalent lab or a non-production GCC tenant** first; scope expectations to the **Identity** tab (the part that works in gov); **ignore Network results** as out-of-cloud noise.
3. Surface the **access + data-handling gates** (Global-Admin consent; local sensitive-data storage) to the tenant owner up front — those, not the install, are what stall it in a federal environment.
